4686   /**
4687    * Returns the variable resolver for this servlet.
4688    *
4689    * <p>
4690    * Variable resolvers are used to replace variables in property values.
4691    * They can be nested arbitrarily deep.
4692    * They can also return values that themselves contain other variables.
4693    *
4694    * <h4 class='figure'>Example:</h4>
4695    * <p class='bjava'>
4696    *    <ja>@Rest</ja>(
4697    *       messages=<js>"nls/Messages"</js>,
4698    *       properties={
4699    *          <ja>@Property</ja>(name=<js>"title"</js>,value=<js>"${L:title}"</js>),  <jc>// Localized variable in Messages.properties</jc>
4700    *          <ja>@Property</ja>(name=<js>"javaVendor"</js>,value=<js>"${S:java.vendor:Oracle}"</js>),  <jc>// System property with default value</jc>
4701    *          <ja>@Property</ja>(name=<js>"foo"</js>,value=<js>"bar"</js>),
4702    *          <ja>@Property</ja>(name=<js>"bar"</js>,value=<js>"baz"</js>),
4703    *          <ja>@Property</ja>(name=<js>"v1"</js>,value=<js>"${R:foo}"</js>),  <jc>// Request variable.  value="bar"</jc>
4704    *          <ja>@Property</ja>(name=<js>"v1"</js>,value=<js>"${R:foo:bar}"</js>),  <jc>// Request variable.  value="bar"</jc>
4705    *       }
4706    *    )
4707    *    <jk>public class</jk> MyRestResource <jk>extends</jk> BasicRestServlet {
4708    * </p>
4709    *
4710    * <p>
4711    * A typical usage pattern involves using variables inside the {@link HtmlDocConfig @HtmlDocConfig} annotation:
4712    * <p class='bjava'>
4713    *    <ja>@RestGet</ja>(<js>"/{name}/*"</js>)
4714    *    <ja>@HtmlDocConfig</ja>(
4715    *       navlinks={
4716    *          <js>"up: ${R:requestParentURI}"</js>,
4717    *          <js>"api: servlet:/api"</js>,
4718    *          <js>"stats: servlet:/stats"</js>,
4719    *          <js>"editLevel: servlet:/editLevel?logger=${A:attribute.name: OFF}"</js>
4720    *       }
4721    *       header={
4722    *          <js>"&lt;h1&gt;${L:MyLocalizedPageTitle}&lt;/h1&gt;"</js>
4723    *       },
4724    *       aside={
4725    *          <js>"${F:resources/AsideText.html}"</js>
4726    *       }
4727    *    )
4728    *    <jk>public</jk> LoggerEntry getLogger(RestRequest <jv>req</jv>, <ja>@Path</ja> String <jv>name</jv>) <jk>throws</jk> Exception {
4729    * </p>
4730    *
4731    * <h4 class='section'>See Also:</h4><ul>
4732    *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerSvlVariables">REST Server SVL Variables</a>
4733    * </ul>
4734    *
4735    * @return The var resolver in use by this resource.
4736    */

5166   /**
5167    * Method that can be subclassed to allow uncaught throwables to be treated as other types of throwables.
5168    *
5169    * <p>
5170    * The default implementation looks at the throwable class name to determine whether it can be converted to another type:
5171    *
5172    * <ul>
5173    *    <li>{@link BeanQuerySyntaxException} - Converted to {@link BadRequest} carrying the exception's message and an
5174    *       {@value BeanQueryRequest#ERROR_HEADER} header set to its {@link BeanQuerySyntaxException#code() code()}.
5175    *    <li>{@link BeanQueryExecutionException} - Converted to {@link InternalServerError} with the generic message
5176    *       <js>"Query execution failed."</js>; the original exception (and its cause) stays attached for logging.
5177    *    <li><js>"*AccessDenied*"</js> - Converted to {@link Unauthorized}.
5178    *    <li><js>"*Empty*"</js>,<js>"*NotFound*"</js> - Converted to {@link NotFound}.
5179    *    <li>Any other exception - Converted to {@link InternalServerError} with the generic message
5180    *       <js>"Internal Server Error."</js>; the original exception stays attached as the cause.
5181    *       Returned unchanged when {@link #isRenderResponseStackTraces()} is enabled, or when the throwable is a
5182    *       problem-details exception, a legacy HTTP response exception, or has a registered {@link ProblemMapper}.
5183    * </ul>
5184    *
5185    * @param t The thrown object.
5186    * @return The converted thrown object.
5187    */
5188   public Throwable convertThrowable(Throwable t) {
5189
5190      if (t instanceof InvocationTargetException t2)
5191         t = t2.getTargetException();
5192
5193      if (t instanceof ExecutableException t2)
5194         t = t2.getTargetException();
5195
5196      if (t instanceof BasicHttpException t2)
5197         return t2;
5198
5199      var ci = ClassInfo.of(t);
5200
5201      if (ci.hasAnnotation(Response.class))
5202         return t;
5203
5204      if (ci.isAssignableTo(ParseException.class) || ci.is(InvalidDataConversionException.class))
5205         return new BadRequest(t);
5206
5207      if (t instanceof BeanQuerySyntaxException e)
5208         return new BadRequest(e).setHeader(BeanQueryRequest.ERROR_HEADER, e.code().name());
5209
5210      // The cause may carry SQL or table names: keep it attached for logging, but never in the client-facing message.
5211      if (t instanceof BeanQueryExecutionException e)
5212         return new InternalServerError(e, "Query execution failed.");
5213
5214      String n = cn(t);
5215
5216      if (co(n, "AccessDenied") || co(n, "Unauthorized"))
5217         return new Unauthorized(t);
5218
5219      if (co(n, "Empty") || co(n, "NotFound"))
5220         return new NotFound(t);
5221
5222      // Any other exception is an unplanned failure: its class name and message were never written for a client audience,
5223      // so hide them behind a generic 500 (the original stays attached as the cause for logging and for RRPC).
5224      if (isRenderResponseStackTraces() || isIntentionalResponse(t))
5225         return t;
5226      return new InternalServerError(t, "Internal Server Error.");
5227   }

5375   /**
5376    * Method for handling response errors.
5377    *
5378    * <p>
5379    * Subclasses can override this method to provide their own custom error response handling.
5380    *
5381    * <p>
5382    * The {@code Thrown} response header and the cause-chain detail normally appended to the error body are both
5383    * gated behind {@link #isRenderResponseStackTraces()} (see {@code @Rest(renderResponseStackTraces)}), which is
5384    * off by default. With that flag off, only a message the calling code deliberately supplied via a thrown
5385    * {@link BasicHttpException} (its subclasses, e.g. {@code NotFound} or {@code BadRequest}) is echoed back;
5386    * the class name and message text of any other, unplanned exception type bubbling up from application code
5387    * is kept out of both the header and the body, since that text was never authored with a client audience in
5388    * mind and may otherwise incidentally carry implementation detail (file paths, driver/database error text,
5389    * and the like). Turn the flag on for local debugging to get the full detail back.
5390    *
5391    * <p>
5392    * The {@code Thrown} header is still always set for RRPC dispatch responses (an operation invoked through
5393    * {@code @RestOp(method=HttpMethod.RRPC)}), regardless of {@link #isRenderResponseStackTraces()}. The RRPC/
5394    * {@code @Remote} client stub has no other channel for learning the server-side exception's class in order to
5395    * reconstruct and rethrow the equivalent type locally, so that one header is part of the RPC contract rather
5396    * than incidental debug detail. The error body's cause-chain message is unaffected by this exemption and
5397    * remains suppressed the same as any other operation.
5398    *
5399    * @param session The rest call.
5400    * @param e The exception that occurred.
5401    * @throws IOException Can be thrown if a problem occurred trying to write to the output stream.
5402    */
5403   protected synchronized void handleError(RestSession session, Throwable e) throws IOException {
5404
5405      // Client disconnected mid-response: routine.  Don't record it, log it, or try to write an error to a dead socket.
5406      if (session.logContainerClientAbort(e))
5407         return;
5408
5409      session.exception(e);
5410
5411      if (getLogger().isLoggable(Level.FINE))
5412         getLogger().log(Level.WARNING, e, () -> "Error occurred during REST call.");
5413
5414      int code = 500;
5415
5416      var ci = ClassInfo.of(e);
5417      var r = ci.getAnnotations(StatusCode.class).findFirst().map(AnnotationInfo::inner).orElse(null);
5418      if (nn(r) && r.value().length > 0)
5419         code = r.value()[0];
5420
5421      var appThrown = e instanceof BasicHttpException;
5422      var e2 = (e instanceof BasicHttpException e3 ? e3 : new BasicHttpException(code, null, e));
5423
5424      var req = session.getRequest();
5425      var res = session.getResponse();
5426
5427      var t2 = resolveThrownHeader(e2, isRenderResponseStackTraces(), isRpcDispatch(session));
5428      if (nn(t2))
5429         res.setHeader(t2.getName(), t2.getValue());
5430
5431      // Matches the op-method path (HttpResponseProcessor / ProblemDetailsProcessor), which sends this header too.
5432      e2.getHeaders().stream()
5433         .filter(h -> BeanQueryRequest.ERROR_HEADER.equals(h.getName()))
5434         .findFirst()
5435         .ifPresent(h -> res.setHeader(h.getName(), h.getValue()));
5436
5437      // RFC 9110 requires Allow on a 405; the framework's own 405s carry it on the exception.
5438      e2.getHeaders().stream()
5439         .filter(h -> eqic("Allow", h.getName()))
5440         .findFirst()
5441         .ifPresent(h -> res.setHeader("Allow", h.getValue()));
5442
5443      try {
5444         var statusCode = e2.getStatusLine().getStatusCode();
5445
5446         if (e2 instanceof ValidationException e3 && writeValidationErrorBody(res, e3, statusCode, isProblemDetails()))
5447            return;
5448
5449         if (isProblemDetails() && writeProblemDetailsBody(res, e2, statusCode))
5450            return;
5451
5452         res.setContentType("text/plain");
5453         res.setHeader("Content-Encoding", "identity");
5454         res.setStatus(statusCode);
5455
5456         PrintWriter w = getResponseWriter(res);
5457
5458         try (PrintWriter w2 = w) {
5459            var httpMessage = RestUtils.getHttpResponseText(statusCode);
5460            if (nn(httpMessage))
5461               w2.append("HTTP ").append(String.valueOf(statusCode)).append(": ").append(httpMessage).append("\n\n");
5462            if (isRenderResponseStackTraces())
5463               e.printStackTrace(w2);
5464            else
5465               w2.append(suppressedErrorBodyMessage(e2, appThrown));
5466         }
5467
5468      } catch (Exception e1) {
5469         req.setAttribute("Exception", e1);
5470      }
5471   }

5473   /**
5474    * Determines the {@code Thrown} response header to set for a reported error, if any.
5475    *
5476    * <p>
5477    * Package-private (rather than folded directly into {@link #handleError(RestSession, Throwable)}) so the
5478    * gating decision can be exercised directly in unit tests without standing up a full request/response cycle.
5479    *
5480    * @param e2 The (possibly wrapped) exception being reported. Must not be {@code null}.
5481    * @param renderResponseStackTraces The resolved {@code renderResponseStackTraces} setting for the call.
5482    * @param rpcDispatch {@code true} if the call being reported on is an RRPC dispatch (see
5483    *    {@link #isRpcDispatch(RestSession)}), in which case the header is included even when
5484    *    {@code renderResponseStackTraces} is off, since the RRPC/{@code @Remote} client depends on it to
5485    *    reconstruct the original exception type.  In that case only the exception class name is included; the
5486    *    message is added only when {@code renderResponseStackTraces} is on.

5495         return null;
5496      if (renderResponseStackTraces)

5498      // RRPC callers need the exception class to rebuild it locally; the message text stays server-side.
5499      return Thrown.of(urlEncode(UnmodifiableBean.logicalType(t).getName()) + ";");
5500   }

5520    * Determines the message written to the plain-text error response body when
5521    * {@code renderResponseStackTraces} is off.
5522    *
5523    * <p>
5524    * Package-private for the same unit-testability reason as {@link #resolveThrownHeader(BasicHttpException, boolean)}.
5525    *
5526    * @param e2 The (possibly wrapped) exception being reported. Must not be {@code null}.
5527    * @param appThrown {@code true} if the original, unwrapped exception was itself a {@link BasicHttpException}
5528    *    (i.e. deliberately thrown by application code with a client-facing message in mind).
5529    * @return The scrubbed message to write, or an empty string if nothing should be written (the exception
5530    *    wasn't application-authored, so its message is treated as internal detail).
5531    */
5532   static String suppressedErrorBodyMessage(BasicHttpException e2, boolean appThrown) {
5533      return appThrown ? scrubForXss(e2.getMessage()) : "";
5534   }
5535
5536   /**
5537    * Replaces {@code <}, {@code >}, and {@code &} in a message about to be written into a {@code text/plain}
5538    * error response body, as a simple defense against the body being reflected into an HTML context downstream.
5539    *
5540    * @param msg The message to scrub. Can be {@code null}.
5541    * @return The scrubbed message, or an empty string if {@code msg} was {@code null}.
5542    */
5543   private static String scrubForXss(String msg) {
5544      return msg == null ? "" : msg.replace('<', ' ').replace('>', ' ').replace('&', ' ');
5545   }
5546
5547   /**
5548    * Writes a {@code BasicHttpException} as an {@code application/problem+json} body. The {@code Accept}
5549    * header is intentionally ignored on the error path so opted-in resources always emit Problem JSON for thrown
5550    * exceptions.
5551    *
5552    * @return {@code true} if the body was written (response committed). {@code false} on serialization failure so
5553    *    the caller can fall back to the legacy {@code text/plain} writer.
5554    */
5555   private static boolean writeProblemDetailsBody(HttpServletResponse res, BasicHttpException e, int statusCode) {
5556      try {
5557         var problem = ProblemAdapters.fromException(e);
5558         e.getHeaders().stream()
5559            .filter(h -> BeanQueryRequest.ERROR_HEADER.equals(h.getName()))
5560            .findFirst()
5561            .ifPresent(h -> problem.set("code", h.getValue()));
5562         res.setStatus(statusCode);
5563         res.setContentType(ContentType.APPLICATION_PROBLEM_JSON.getValue());
5564         res.setHeader("Content-Encoding", "identity");
5565         var os = res.getOutputStream();
5566         Json.DEFAULT.write(problem, os);
5567         os.flush();
5568         return true;
5569      } catch (Exception ex) {
5570         return false;
5571      }
5572   }
5573
5574   /**
5575    * Writes a {@link ValidationException} as a structured JSON body carrying the per-field
5576    * {@link ValidationViolation} list, so client UIs can render field-level errors.
5577    *
5578    * <p>
5579    * Two shapes depending on the resource's {@code @Rest(problemDetails)} opt-in:
5580    * <ul class='spaced-list'>
5581    *    <li><b>Problem-details ON</b> &mdash; emits {@code application/problem+json} with the standard
5582    *       RFC 7807 {@code status}/{@code title}/{@code detail} members plus an {@code errors[]} extension
5583    *       array populated from {@link ValidationException#getViolations()}. Bypasses the generic
5584    *       {@link ProblemAdapters#fromException(BasicHttpException)} path because that adapter is
5585    *       intentionally narrow (no extensions) &mdash; validation needs its own per-field payload.
5586    *    <li><b>Problem-details OFF (default)</b> &mdash; emits {@code application/json} with the simple
5587    *       {@code { "status":400, "errors":[ ... ] }} envelope. Keeps the response usable from clients that
5588    *       can't parse {@code application/problem+json} without making validation responses look like a
5589    *       text/plain stack trace.
5590    * </ul>
5591    *
5592    * @return {@code true} if the body was written (response committed). {@code false} on serialization
5593    *    failure so the caller can fall back to the legacy {@code text/plain} writer.
5594    */
5595   private static boolean writeValidationErrorBody(HttpServletResponse res, ValidationException ve, int statusCode, boolean problemDetails) {
5596      try {
5597         res.setStatus(statusCode);
5598         res.setHeader("Content-Encoding", "identity");
5599         var os = res.getOutputStream();
5600         if (problemDetails) {
5601            var problem = new Problem()
5602               .setStatus(statusCode)
5603               .setTitle(ve.getStatusLine().getReasonPhrase())
5604               .setDetail(ve.getMessage())
5605               .set("errors", ve.getViolations());
5606            res.setContentType(ContentType.APPLICATION_PROBLEM_JSON.getValue());
5607            Json.DEFAULT.write(problem, os);
5608         } else {
5609            var envelope = new LinkedHashMap<String,Object>();
5610            envelope.put("status", statusCode);
5611            envelope.put("errors", ve.getViolations());
5612            res.setContentType("application/json");
5613            Json.DEFAULT.write(envelope, os);
5614         }
5615         os.flush();
5616         return true;
5617      } catch (Exception ex) {
5618         return false;
5619      }
5620   }
5621
5622   private static PrintWriter getResponseWriter(HttpServletResponse res) throws IOException {
5623      try {
5624         return res.getWriter();
5625      } catch (@SuppressWarnings("unused") IllegalStateException x) {
5626         return new PrintWriter(new OutputStreamWriter(res.getOutputStream(), UTF8));
5627      }
5628   }

5630   protected void handleNotFound(RestSession session) throws Exception {
5631      var pathInfo = session.getPathInfo();
5632      var methodUC = session.getMethod();
5633      var rc = session.getStatus();
5634      var onPath = pathInfo == null ? " on no pathInfo" : (" on path '" + pathInfo + "'");
5635      if (rc == SC_NOT_FOUND)
5636         throw new NotFound("Method '%s' not found on resource with matching pattern%s.", methodUC, onPath);
5637      else if (rc == SC_PRECONDITION_FAILED)
5638         throw new PreconditionFailed("Method '%s' not found on resource%s with matching matcher.", methodUC, onPath);
5639      else if (rc == SC_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED) {
5640         var e = new MethodNotAllowed("Method '%s' not found on resource%s.", methodUC, onPath);
5641         e.setHeader("Allow", getRestOperations().allowedMethods(session));
5642         throw e;
5643      }
5644      else if (rc < SC_BAD_REQUEST)
5645         // Reaching this method means no operation matched, so a still-successful or unset status must resolve to a
5646         // 404 rather than a 500.  Under a real servlet container the response status defaults to 200 (never the
5647         // mock response's coincidental 0), so throwing "Invalid method response" for a non-error status would turn
5648         // every unmatched path into an HTTP 500 in production while staying invisible to the mock-based tests.
5649         throw new NotFound("Method '%s' not found on resource with matching pattern%s.", methodUC, onPath);
5650      else if (rc < SC_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR)
5651         // A start-call hook left another client-error status (e.g. 400, 401, 403, 409) and nothing matched:
5652         // keep that status rather than converting it to a 500.
5653         throw new BasicHttpException(rc, null, "Method '%s' not found on resource%s.", methodUC, onPath);
5654      else
5655         throw new ServletException("Invalid method response: " + rc, session.getException());
5656   }

5658   /**
5659    * Called during a request to invoke all {@link RestPostCall} methods.
5660    *
5661    * <p>
5662    * For mixin-endpoint requests, fires the host's {@code @RestPostCall} methods first (via the host's
5663    * {@code localPostCallInvokers}), then the mixin's per-op invokers ({@link RestOpContext#getPostCallMethods()}).
5664    * Host-endpoint requests fire only the host's per-op invokers (the established path; unchanged from pre-10.0.0).
5665    *
5666    * @param session The current request.
5667    * @throws Exception If thrown from call methods.
5668    */
5669   protected void postCall(RestOpSession session) throws Exception {
5670      var opCtx = session.getContext().getContext();
5671      if (opCtx.isMixinContext && opCtx.parentContext != null)
5672         for (var m : opCtx.parentContext.localPostCallInvokers.get())
5673            m.invoke(session);
5674      for (var m : session.getContext().getPostCallMethods())
5675         m.invoke(session);
5676   }
5677
5678   /**
5679    * Called during a request to invoke all {@link RestPreCall} methods.
5680    *
5681    * <p>
5682    * For mixin-endpoint requests, fires the host's {@code @RestPreCall} methods first (via the host's
5683    * {@code localPreCallInvokers}), then the mixin's per-op invokers ({@link RestOpContext#getPreCallMethods()}).
5684    * Host-endpoint requests fire only the host's per-op invokers (the established path; unchanged from pre-10.0.0).
5685    *
5686    * @param session The current request.
5687    * @throws Exception If thrown from call methods.
5688    */
5689   protected void preCall(RestOpSession session) throws Exception {
5690      var opCtx = session.getContext().getContext();
5691      if (opCtx.isMixinContext && opCtx.parentContext != null)
5692         for (var m : opCtx.parentContext.localPreCallInvokers.get())
5693            m.invoke(session);
5694      for (var m : session.getContext().getPreCallMethods())
5695         m.invoke(session);
5696   }

5698   /**
5699    * The main method for serializing POJOs passed in through the {@link RestResponse#setContent(Object)} method or
5700    * returned by the Java method.
5701    *
5702    * <p>
5703    * Subclasses may override this method if they wish to modify the way the output is rendered or support other output
5704    * formats.
5705    *
5706    * <p>
5707    * The default implementation simply iterates through the response handlers on this resource
5708    * looking for the first one whose {@link ResponseProcessor#process(RestOpSession)} method returns
5709    * <jk>true</jk>.
5710    *
5711    * @param opSession The HTTP call.
5712    * @throws IOException Thrown by underlying stream.
5713    * @throws BasicHttpException Non-200 response.
5714    * @throws NotImplemented No registered response processors could handle the call.
5715    */
5716   @SuppressWarnings({
5717      "java:S127" // Loop counter i resets to -1 on RESTART
5718   })
5719   public void processResponse(RestOpSession opSession) throws IOException, BasicHttpException, NotImplemented {
5720
5721      // Loop until we find the correct processor for the POJO.
5722      int loops = 5;
5723      var rp = getResponseProcessors();
5724      for (var i = 0; i < rp.length; i++) {
5725         var j = rp[i].process(opSession);
5726         if (j == FINISHED)
5727            return;
5728         if (j == RESTART) {
5729            if (loops-- < 0)
5730               throw new InternalServerError("Too many processing loops.");
5731            i = -1;  // Start over.
5732         }
5733      }
5734
5735      var output = opSession.getResponse().getContent().orElse(null);
5736      throw new NotImplemented("No response processors found to process output of type '%s'", cn(output));
5737   }

5769   /**
5770    * Called at the start of a request to invoke all {@link RestStartCall} methods on this context.
5771    *
5772    * <p>
5773    * Fires this context's own {@code @RestStartCall} methods against its own resource instance. The host
5774    * version is invoked from {@link #execute(Object, HttpServletRequest, HttpServletResponse)} before the
5775    * operation is resolved; once the operation is known to belong to a mixin sub-context,
5776    * {@link RestSession#run()} additionally calls {@code startCall} on the mixin context so host hooks fire
5777    * first, then the mixin's.
5778    *
5779    * @param session The current request.
5780    * @throws BasicHttpException If thrown from call methods.
5781    */
5782   protected void startCall(RestSession session) throws BasicHttpException {
5783      for (var x : startCallInvokerPair.get().invokers) {
5784         try {
5785            x.invoke(session.getBeanStore(), getResource());
5786         } catch (IllegalAccessException | IllegalArgumentException e) {
5787            throw new InternalServerError(e, "Error occurred invoking start-call method '%s'.", x.getFullName());
5788         } catch (InvocationTargetException e) {
5789            var t = e.getTargetException();
5790            if (t instanceof BasicHttpException t2)
5791               throw t2;
5792            throw new InternalServerError(t);
5793         }
5794      }
5795   }
